claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to load_creds, resolve_creds_env over the name forms this pass searched

load_creds and resolve_creds_env take no argument. resolve_creds_env returns a dict holding only the JIRA_BASE_URL, JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN fields that resolved, per field from exported variables, then ~/.claude.json, then ~/.codex/config.toml; a read or parse error is swallowed and it never exits.

load_creds calls resolve_creds_env, exits through sys.exit(message) when fewer than 3 fields resolve, and otherwise returns the tuple (JIRA_BASE_URL with trailing slashes stripped, JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN).

The direct callers of load_creds are api.py:464 client(), api.py:649 --check-creds, publish_prd.py:267, publish_meeting.py:128 and publish_bug.py:299 _connect(); each publisher unpacks the 3 values positionally into Jira(base, email, token).

The direct callers of resolve_creds_env are api.py:131 load_creds, afk-config.py:955 (presence of JIRA_BASE_URL only, for the init hint) and developer_values.py:116 (JIRA_EMAIL only, as the trackerAssignee suggestion; any Exception becomes None).

client() is called only by _json (api.py:481); every one of the nine operations reaches _json through the _DISPATCH table and call(); call() is reached from the tracker MCP server's _call (server.py:101) behind nine @mcp.tool() functions and from the api.py CLI main (api.py:664).

In the tool and CLI path a load_creds exit does not end the process: SystemExit passes through _json's except Exception and is caught in call(), which answers {error: true, operation, reason: <exit message>}; server._call adds config_root and the CLI prints the JSON with exit 0.

In the --check-creds path and in all three publishers nothing catches the SystemExit: the process ends with exit status 1 and the load_creds message on stderr; publish_bug's main catches only BugPublishError and OSError.

publish_prd and publish_meeting resolve credentials even with --dry-run (load_creds runs before the dry-run test); publish_bug's transition, comment and backfill dry-runs, and its create dry-run, return before _connect().

Publishers reach api.py through tracker_api.load, which picks adapters/tracker/<kind>/api.py from tracker: in .afk/config.yaml and exits naming the missing attributes when the kind lacks them; only the jira kind defines load_creds. afk-config.py and developer_values.py load the jira adapter by fixed path whatever the configured tracker.

The Jira site address is read today from exactly 3 sources, all inside resolve_creds_env: the JIRA_BASE_URL variable, the env block of the tracker (or afk-owned legacy jira) server found by a recursive walk of ~/.claude.json, and the same block in ~/.codex/config.toml mcp_servers. Jira prefixes it to every relative REST path.

setup_secrets.py reads its prompt default for the site address only from the top-level ~/.claude.json mcpServers.tracker (or afk's legacy jira) env block, requires https://, validates with GET <base>/rest/api/3/myself, and writes the three keys back into that block; it reads no exported variable and no Codex file, and no code writes the Codex tracker env block.

The config key jira.credentials-env is never read for its value: its code sites are the schema allowlist, a list-type check, scaffold comments and the adapter manifest; no code hard-codes a Jira host (the only atlassian.net code hit is the setup prompt placeholder).

The CLI, publish_bug, publish_prd and publish_meeting exit with the message. afk-config catches only ImportError at load (afk-config.py:953); developer_values catches every Exception and returns None (developer_values.py:117).

setup_secrets.py reads the Jira site address without resolve_creds_env: it takes JIRA_BASE_URL, JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN defaults from the ~/.claude.json top-level tracker entry (or afk's own legacy jira entry) through tracker_registration.prior_env (setup_secrets.py:185-208, tracker_registration.py:52-56), ignoring exported variables, ~/.codex/config.toml and nested project blocks; it calls GET <base>/rest/api/3/myself (setup_secrets.py:223-228), writes the triple into that entry (239-252), and re-probes presence by reading ~/.claude.json mcpServers.tracker.env directly (296-305).
